rule: `implicit`: an execution edge the language runs without a written call — `Type#<clinit>` → `Type#field` (static initializer), `Type#<init>` → `Type#field` (instance field initializer). | C3 Operation classification. Each written construct is exactly one of: an invocation ...; a dynamic invocation, meaning a call through a value: `callback`, unknown; ...; implicit execution: `implicit`; ...
source: KNOWN_GAP: range-over-func loop bodies (for x := range seq) get no edges
spec_gap: Does `for x := range seq` (range-over-func, Go 1.23) emit an edge for the iterator invocation the language performs without a written call, seq(yield) — and if so which: callback/unknown to `seq` (a call through a function value), `implicit`, or for `range Count(3)` a low/VTA edge to the returned closure example.com/m.Count$1 — or no edge at all? Separately, is the caller of calls written in the loop body (process(x), fmt.Println(y)) the enclosing function example.com/m.Sum (the body is not a function literal in the source) or the compiler-synthesized yield closure? The body calls themselves are clearly required edges (process high, fmt.Println medium, Count high), but the case cannot be stated completely until the iterator-invocation question is ruled.
notes: Inside Count's closure (Count$1), yield(i) is a call through a parameter: callback `yield`, unknown — decidable, but the case as a whole is not.
